# DATproof

> DATproof is a free daily data feed, for anyone with idle cash and the AI they ask, on where
> idle US-dollar cash can sit: three bitcoin-backed preferred stocks (STRC, SATA, SATS) that pay
> a dividend every business day, beside savings, CDs, a money market fund and T-bills. Every number carries its source and the date it is true
> for. It informs and does arithmetic; it never chooses for anyone, holds no money and places no
> orders. Not advice.

Figures below are from the feed dated 28 Nov 2026 and are rebuilt every day.

## Page (today's figures written into the text, no script needed)

- https://datproof.com/ : yields beside savings, CDs, a money market fund and T-bills; past results; a bitcoin crash test; what can go wrong; a "your situation" worked example; where to buy; questions.
- https://datproof.com/index.md : the same page as Markdown.

## Today

- STRC, SATA and SATS pay 12.2% to 16.9% a year at today's prices.
- High-yield savings pays 4.40% (28 Nov 2026); a 4-week T-bill 4.19%.
- STRC and SATA: variable rate, which the issuers say they adjust to keep the price near $100; SATS: fixed 15% rate, price free to move.
- Past year, dividends plus price change: STRC +14.1% and SATA +11.0%.
- Example, from today's feed: $8,000 for three months, before tax, dividends only: STRC $241, SATA $283 and SATS $334; high-yield savings would earn about $87.
- The price moves and tends to move with bitcoin. For cash that can sit three months or more.

## Data

- https://datproof.com/v1/instruments.json : every instrument, comparison rate and broker link, with sources and dates.
- https://datproof.com/v1/method.json : every formula in plain words.
- https://datproof.com/v1/scenarios.json : what a sum of cash did over past windows.

## Plug-in (MCP server)

    claude mcp add datproof -- uvx --from git+https://github.com/lucascashwell3-ai/datproof@57d06d3e2eea13eb3b61c3a2ee8e6f028429c8c8 datproof-mcp

Seven read-only tools: compare, instrument, instruments, changes, scenarios, method and check.

The compare tool takes an amount, how long the cash will sit (1 month, 3 months, 6 months, 1 year) and
where it sits now, and returns the same rows for STRC, SATA and SATS, plus brokers' pages for each.

The check tool takes one ticker, an optional amount and the owner's own limits (lowest yield, highest
price, lowest backing, biggest past-year fall, largest share of a day's trading, the oldest any figure
may be, a current dividend). It returns each fact with its date and source, and for each limit: pass,
fail, no limit set, or cannot tell when the fact is missing, undated or too old. The age limit applies
to every figure behind a check: any figure older than it reads cannot tell, and figures from company
filings (debt, for instance) can be weeks old. A current dividend fails on a missed payment or when the
last payment is overdue for the issue's own pay schedule, and reads cannot tell when the schedule or a
date is unknown. It compares facts with limits the owner set; it is not advice and places no order.
